hypothesis: A surah's own letters are unusually frequent within it (rasm rung)
note: Primary pre-specified test. Effect is carried by a subset: dropping the 3 strongest surahs gives p=0.067.
Effect is near-flat across rungs; rasm marginally strongest.

hypothesis: Muqatta'at surahs announce scripture in their opening verses
note: Survives length matching. Pre-specified root set; a broader set would raise it to 29/29 but that is post-hoc.

hypothesis: Muqatta'at surahs cluster in mushaf order
stat: 10 runs vs 16.6 expected under a length-matched null
note: Survives controlling for the mushaf's rough length ordering.

hypothesis: Surahs sharing an opening are lexically alike, beyond adjacency
note: Restricted to pairs >3 surahs apart, so adjacency cannot explain it. n=16 same-opening pairs.

hypothesis: Muqatta'at surahs are more ambiguous when undotted
note: Raw effect p=0.0001 shrinks to p=0.013 once word length is controlled. Interpretation unclear.

hypothesis: Mim specifically is enriched in the 17 surahs whose opening contains it
note: One of 6 letters tested; does not survive correction within that sub-family.

hypothesis: The seven consecutive ha-mim surahs are unusually cohesive
note: An earlier run gave p=0.003 against a null of random non-adjacent surahs. That null was wrong.

hypothesis: The 14 openings nest (prefix/subset structure) beyond chance
note: Pattern is visible but within chance.

hypothesis: A surah's opening letters match its dominant rhyme letter
note: Clean refutation. 18/29 of these surahs rhyme in nun regardless.

hypothesis: The 14 letters systematically cover the points of articulation
stat: 9 of 12 places vs 9.2 for a random 14 letters
note: Interdentals, labiodentals and laterals are entirely absent.

hypothesis: The letters are denser near the start of their surah
note: Argues against an attention-getter or phonetic-prelude reading.

hypothesis: The 14 letters are a biased sample of the alphabet
note: They skew toward COMMON letters: 10 of the alphabet's 14 commonest are used. But ta (rank 28) and sad (24) are included.

hypothesis: Own-letter counts are divisible by 19 more often than chance
note: Approximate; the 19-based literature is not supported here.

hypothesis: Muqatta'at surahs are more textually stable across riwayat
